title: PHP Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: A first message
examples.description: echo shows text. Text is a string: a row of letters inside quotes.

examples.title: Named values
examples.description: A variable keeps a value under a name. PHP variable names start with a dollar sign.

examples.title: Join pieces of text
examples.description: The dot joins text in PHP. Joining is called concatenation.

examples.title: Choose a message
examples.description: if checks a rule. The >= sign means at least.

examples.title: Store a short list
examples.description: An array can keep values in order. Its first numbered position is zero.

examples.title: Visit each item
examples.description: foreach repeats its block for every item in an array.

examples.title: Name a set of steps
examples.description: A function takes an input and can return a result. return sends the answer back.
examples.code:
<?php
function twice(int $n): int { return $n * 2; }
echo twice(4);

examples.title: Look up a named value
examples.description: An array can use text keys. A key is a label used to find a value.

examples.title: Check value and type
examples.description: The === test checks both the value and its type. Text 5 is not the same type as number 5.

examples.title: Choose a fallback
examples.description: The ?? operator uses a fallback when a value is missing or null.

examples.title: Make JSON text
examples.description: JSON is a text format for data. json_encode turns this small array into JSON.

examples.title: Keep data in an object
examples.description: A class is a plan for objects. Each object can have its own stored fields.
examples.code:
<?php
class Badge { public string $colour = "blue"; }
$badge = new Badge();
echo $badge->colour;
